VIDEO.title: Paul Says YOU Are the Sacrifice
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 12:1-8 · Episode 20 (#20 of 28 in the playlist)
SUMMARY: The teacher opens: most Christians think sacrifice ended at the cross. 'Christ isn't sacrificed again, you are.' He reads Romans 12:1-8: present your bodies as a living sacrifice (12:1); do not be conformed but transformed (12:2); do not think too highly of yourself, but with sound thinking, by the measure of faith God has allotted (12:3); one body with many members and differing gifts (12:4-8).

Review of Romans 1-11: Paul was never writing a systematic textbook but stepping into a clash between Jewish-background and Gentile-background Christians. All are guilty (1-3); God remains faithful (3:1-4); Abraham is father of all who believe (4); believers move from the reign of sin to the reign of grace (5-6); death ends Torah's jurisdiction (7); the Spirit marks new covenant life (8); Israel's stumbling is not final, and the olive tree is covenant continuity, not replacement (9-11).

'Therefore' (12:1) gathers up everything in Romans 1-11, and 'the mercies of God' sums it up. Paul moves from indicatives to imperatives: what God has done, then how the church must respond (12-16). The video quotes Robert Mounce on God's ethical instruction arising from who He is and what He has done.

Paul uses temple language: present, sacrifice, acceptable, worship. Latreia is temple service, so your daily life is temple service to God, embodied obedience rather than isolated acts of devotion. To a Jewish listener this is shocking: instead of animals offered in Jerusalem, God receives the lives of His people. Romans 6:13 and 8:9-11 laid the groundwork. Verse 2 allows no neutral ground: conforming or transforming.

'A measure of faith' (12:3): with Dwight Pryor, the teacher reads it as the God-assigned sphere in which one's faith is expressed through service, as 12:4-8 shows. Christians should neither inflate nor despise their role.

Old Testament background: Leviticus 1:3-4 (accepted before Yahweh); obedience as the heart of sacrifice (Hosea 6:6, quoted in Matthew 12:7; Psalm 51:16-17; Psalm 141:2; 1 Samuel 15:22; Proverbs 21:3; also Isaiah 1:11-17 and Micah 6:6-8); resisting the nations' patterns (Leviticus 18:3); a new heart (Ezekiel 36:26-27); wisdom leading to the knowledge of God (Proverbs 2:1-6); a kingdom of priests (Exodus 19:5-6); Bezalel filled with the Spirit (Exodus 31:2-3; 35:30-35).

Covenant renewal: Israel's leaders rehearsed God's saving acts, then called the people to loyalty (Deuteronomy 29-30; Joshua 24; Nehemiah 8-10). Romans follows the same logic, though Paul is not cutting a new covenant. The lesson: 'Because of God's mercy, a transformed people offer their lives to him and serve one another humbly according to the roles that he has given them.'
QUOTES: Because of God's mercy, a transformed people offer their lives to him and serve one another humbly according to the roles that he has given them.
Christ isn't sacrificed again, you are.
Your daily life equals temple service to God.
A lot of us in the church know what we were saved from, but not many of us know what we were saved for.

method.p: In Romans 12:1-2, circle every word that belongs in a temple: present, sacrifice, holy, pleasing, service of worship. Then list the seven gifts in 12:6-8 and put your initials beside the one closest to how God has used you.

LSB_QUOTES.text: Therefore I exhort you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a sacrifice—living, holy, and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may approve what the will of God is, that which is good and pleasing and perfect.
For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.

left.text: ‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall bring it near, a male without blemish; he shall bring it near to the doorway of the tent of meeting, that he may be accepted before Yahweh. ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, that it may be accepted for him to make atonement on his behalf.

right.text: Therefore I exhort you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a sacrifice—living, holy, and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.

lines.text: Offer or present, an acceptable offering, presented to God: the same pattern runs through Leviticus 3:1, 19:5 and 22:29. Paul's logikē latreia ('reasonable service') uses the word for temple service. Instead of animals offered in Jerusalem, God now receives the lives of His people offered in obedience.

left.text: For I delight in lovingkindness rather than sacrifice, / And in the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

right.text: For You do not delight in sacrifice, otherwise I would give it; / You are not pleased with burnt offering. / The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; / A broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.

lines.text: Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6 against the religious leaders (Matthew 12:7). The point was not to abolish sacrifice but to show obedience is its true heart. See also Isaiah 1:11-17 and Micah 6:6-8.

Prayer becomes sacrifice: 'The lifting up of my hands as the evening offering' (Psalm 141:2). 'Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice' (1 Samuel 15:22). Righteousness and justice are 'chosen by Yahweh over sacrifice' (Proverbs 21:3).

src.text: and do not go on presenting your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.

lines.text: Paul said this before, slightly differently. He also laid the groundwork in Romans 8, where the Spirit of God dwells in believers: 'you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you' (Romans 8:9), and see 8:10-11.
Under the new covenant, even Gentiles can offer to God without becoming Jews or entering the Torah covenant, which appears to underlie the church clash.

left.text: You shall not do according to what is done in the land of Egypt where you lived, nor are you to do according to what is done in the land of Canaan where I am bringing you; you shall not walk in their statutes.

right.text: And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may approve what the will of God is, that which is good and pleasing and perfect.

lines.text: Israel was to resist the patterns of the surrounding nations while living among them. A person is either conforming or transforming in daily life; the verse allows no neutral middle ground. Verse 2 is the outflowing of verse 1.

src.text: Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will be careful to do My judgments.

lines.text: Renewal of the mind resonates with God's new covenant promise. Paul draws on the prophets' language of inner renewal for covenant transformation; today we call it sanctification. The video quotes Leon Morris: renewal enables discernment of God's will and sets the believer to doing it.

left.text: If you seek her as silver / And search for her as for hidden treasures; / Then you will understand the fear of Yahweh / And find the knowledge of God.

right.text: For Yahweh gives wisdom; / From His mouth come knowledge and discernment.

lines.text: Renewal leads to discernment of God's will, echoing the wisdom tradition in which God's wisdom leads to knowing God. Mind renewal is about living morally amid the pattern of a corrupt age.

src.text: For through the grace given to me I say to each one among you not to think more highly of himself than he ought to think; but to think so as to have sound thinking, as God has allotted to each a measure of faith.

lines.text: 'Through the grace given to me': God's grace made Paul an apostle with authority. Translation: be humble and understand your role in the church and the kingdom. With Dwight Pryor, 'measure of faith' is the God-assigned sphere where faith is expressed in service, as 12:4-8 shows. Neither inflate nor despise your role.

left.text: So now then, if you will indeed listen to My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be My treasured possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine; and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’

right.text: For just as we have many members in one body and all the members do not have the same function, so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another,

lines.text: Israel was one covenant people with a corporate vocation and many roles: priests, Levites, kings, prophets, judges, teachers of Torah. Paul reframes the roles as prophecy, service, teaching, exhortation, generosity, leadership and mercy (12:6-8).

left.text: “See, I have called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. And I have filled him with the Spirit of God in wisdom, in discernment, in knowledge, and in all kinds of craftsmanship,

right.text: but having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, in agreement with the faith;

lines.text: God distributes abilities among His people for communal purposes: divine calling, Spirit empowerment, different skills, a shared purpose, the building of the sanctuary (see also Exodus 35:30-35).

TERMS.def: A whole life presented to God in daily obedience (12:1).
'Reasonable' or 'spiritual service of worship'; latreia is temple service.
What God has done (Romans 1-11), then how His people must respond (Romans 12-16).
Covenant transformation; the renewal of the mind (12:2).
In the video, the God-assigned sphere where faith is expressed in service (12:3).

BACKGROUND.p: Paul's first hearers knew sacrifice from both sides: the temple in Jerusalem was still standing when he wrote, and Roman religion offered animals at public altars. Calling a living person a sacrifice would have struck both groups.
The burnt offering (Leviticus 1) was wholly burned on the altar, nothing kept back. The worshiper laid his hand on its head 'that it may be accepted for him' (Leviticus 1:4).
Moses on the plains of Moab (Deuteronomy 29-30), Joshua at Shechem (Joshua 24) and Ezra and Nehemiah in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 8-10) each rehearsed God's acts and called for renewed loyalty.

WITNESSES.text: Let the eye look upon no evil thing, and it has become a sacrifice; let your tongue speak nothing filthy, and it has become an offering; let your hand do no lawless deed, and it has become a whole burnt offering.

DEBATES.p: Logikos can mean rational, fitting, or spiritual (as opposed to material offerings). Translations divide: 'reasonable service', 'spiritual worship', 'spiritual service of worship' (LSB). The video stresses daily embodied obedience.
The God-assigned sphere of service (the video, with Pryor); saving faith given equally to all; or a varying degree of faith given for one's gift (Chrysostom calls it 'the gift by faith').

The video sees Romans following the Old Testament renewal pattern (God's acts, then response), while warning not to press it: Paul is not cutting a new covenant. Others read the 'therefore' simply as Paul's usual move from doctrine to ethics.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video says 'look at verse 2' for Bezalel being 'filled with the spirit of God'; the calling is Exodus 31:2 and the filling is 31:3.
The video reads 'So, glorify God in your body' as part of 1 Corinthians 6:19; that line is 6:20.
The captions spell the scholars 'Robert Mounts' and 'Dwight Prior'; the names are Robert Mounce and Dwight Pryor.
The video's Exodus 19:5-6 stresses 'treasured possession singular' and 'kingdom singular of priests'; those are the teacher's emphases, not words in the text.

TIMELINE.what: Sinai: a kingdom of priests; Bezalel builds the tabernacle
David: a broken and contrite heart
Nehemiah: the law read and the covenant renewed

QUESTIONS: What changes if your daily life, not just your quiet time, is temple service?
Where are you conforming without noticing?
Which 'mercies of God' from Romans 1-11 move you most toward obedience?
Do you tend to inflate or despise your role? Why?
Do you know what you were saved for, not only what you were saved from?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: Paul reminds the church that their lives are not their own (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Grace is for good works God prepared beforehand (Ephesians 2:10), and it extends to the roles He gives. The teacher traces his own assignments: a couple of years removed from being an obnoxious atheist, he taught apologetics to a youth group and caught the teaching bug; he became a public high school teacher in Las Vegas, then a pastoral intern, then a pastor; a dream led his family to Tennessee for full-time ministry. A senior pastor once told him, 'Nate, I don't know what to do with you.' Through pain and betrayal, God broke him to fill him with humility, and he is only now understanding Romans 12:3.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): write down one role God has given you this season (at home, church or work). Next to it, write one way to serve in it this week with 'sound thinking' (12:3): neither inflating nor despising it.

3. Proverbs 2:1-6: Testing God's will
   Solomon (Proverbs 2:4-5, LSB): "If you seek her as silver / And search for her as for hidden treasures; / Then you will understand the fear of Yahweh / And find the knowledge of God."
   Solomon (Proverbs 2:6, LSB): "For Yahweh gives wisdom; / From His mouth come knowledge and discernment."
   (video) Renewal leads to discernment of God's will, echoing the wisdom tradition in which God's wisdom leads to knowing God. Mind renewal is about living morally amid the pattern of a corrupt age.

## The measure of faith
1. Romans 12:3: The measure of faith
   Sound thinking Romans 12:3: "For through the grace given to me I say to each one among you not to think more highly of himself than he ought to think; but to think so as to have sound thinking, as God has allotted to each a measure of faith." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+12:3
   (video) 'Through the grace given to me': God's grace made Paul an apostle with authority. Translation: be humble and understand your role in the church and the kingdom. With Dwight Pryor, 'measure of faith' is the God-assigned sphere where faith is expressed in service, as 12:4-8 shows. Neither inflate nor despise your role.
2. Romans 12:4-8; Exodus 19:5-6: One body, many members
   Yahweh (Exodus 19:5-6, LSB): "So now then, if you will indeed listen to My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be My treasured possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine; and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’"
   Paul (Romans 12:4-5, LSB): "For just as we have many members in one body and all the members do not have the same function, so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another,"
   (video) Israel was one covenant people with a corporate vocation and many roles: priests, Levites, kings, prophets, judges, teachers of Torah. Paul reframes the roles as prophecy, service, teaching, exhortation, generosity, leadership and mercy (12:6-8). (Romans 12:6-8)
3. Romans 12:6; Exodus 31:2-3: Gifts that differ
   Yahweh (Exodus 31:2-3, LSB): "“See, I have called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. And I have filled him with the Spirit of God in wisdom, in discernment, in knowledge, and in all kinds of craftsmanship,"
   Paul (Romans 12:6, LSB): "but having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, in agreement with the faith;"
   (video) God distributes abilities among His people for communal purposes: divine calling, Spirit empowerment, different skills, a shared purpose, the building of the sanctuary (see also Exodus 35:30-35). (Exodus 35:30-35)

## Key people
- Bezalel: Called by name and filled with the Spirit of God for the tabernacle work (Exodus 31:2-3). [Background] Of the tribe of Judah, grandson of Hur; he made the ark (Exodus 37:1).
- Joshua: Renewed the covenant: 'choose for yourselves today whom you will serve' (Joshua 24:15). [Background] Moses' successor; the renewal took place at Shechem (Joshua 24:1).
- Nehemiah: Returned exiles heard the law, repented and recommitted (Nehemiah 8-10). [Background] Governor of Judah in the Persian period (Nehemiah 8:9).
- Samuel: 'To obey is better than sacrifice' (1 Samuel 15:22). [Background] Prophet who rebuked King Saul for partial obedience (1 Samuel 15).
- Robert Mounce and Leon Morris: Quoted from their Romans commentaries on ethics flowing from God's acts and on renewal leading to discernment. [Background] Twentieth-century New Testament scholars.
- Dwight Pryor: The teacher agrees with him that the measure of faith is the God-assigned sphere of service. [Background] American Bible teacher (d. 2011) known for studies of the Jewish background of Jesus.

## Places [Background]
- Jerusalem (named in the video): Where animals were offered at the temple; God now receives His people's lives.
- Mount Sinai: A kingdom of priests (Exodus 19:5-6); Bezalel's tabernacle work (Exodus 31). Traditional site.
- Shechem: Joshua's covenant renewal (Joshua 24:1).
- Egypt (named in the video): 'You shall not do according to what is done in the land of Egypt' (Leviticus 18:3).
- Rome (named in the video): The church Paul exhorts by the mercies of God.
- Corinth: Where Paul probably wrote Romans; 'your body is a sanctuary' (1 Corinthians 6:19).

## Key terms
- Living sacrifice: A whole life presented to God in daily obedience (12:1).
- Logikē latreia: 'Reasonable' or 'spiritual service of worship'; latreia is temple service.
- Indicative and imperative: What God has done (Romans 1-11), then how His people must respond (Romans 12-16).
- Sanctification: Covenant transformation; the renewal of the mind (12:2).
- Measure of faith: In the video, the God-assigned sphere where faith is expressed in service (12:3).
- Covenant renewal: Rehearsing God's acts, then calling His people to loyalty (Deuteronomy 29-30; Joshua 24; Nehemiah 8-10).
- Spiritual gifts: Abilities given by grace for the good of the body (12:6-8).

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Sacrifice in Rome: Paul's first hearers knew sacrifice from both sides: the temple in Jerusalem was still standing when he wrote, and Roman religion offered animals at public altars. Calling a living person a sacrifice would have struck both groups.
- The burnt offering: The burnt offering (Leviticus 1) was wholly burned on the altar, nothing kept back. The worshiper laid his hand on its head 'that it may be accepted for him' (Leviticus 1:4).
- Covenant renewal ceremonies: Moses on the plains of Moab (Deuteronomy 29-30), Joshua at Shechem (Joshua 24) and Ezra and Nehemiah in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 8-10) each rehearsed God's acts and called for renewed loyalty.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- 'Spiritual' or 'reasonable' worship? (12:1) Logikos can mean rational, fitting, or spiritual (as opposed to material offerings). Translations divide: 'reasonable service', 'spiritual worship', 'spiritual service of worship' (LSB). The video stresses daily embodied obedience.
- What is 'a measure of faith'? (12:3) The God-assigned sphere of service (the video, with Pryor); saving faith given equally to all; or a varying degree of faith given for one's gift (Chrysostom calls it 'the gift by faith').
- Covenant renewal pattern The video sees Romans following the Old Testament renewal pattern (God's acts, then response), while warning not to press it: Paul is not cutting a new covenant. Others read the 'therefore' simply as Paul's usual move from doctrine to ethics.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video says 'look at verse 2' for Bezalel being 'filled with the spirit of God'; the calling is Exodus 31:2 and the filling is 31:3.
- The video reads 'So, glorify God in your body' as part of 1 Corinthians 6:19; that line is 6:20.
- The captions spell the scholars 'Robert Mounts' and 'Dwight Prior'; the names are Robert Mounce and Dwight Pryor.
- The video's Exodus 19:5-6 stresses 'treasured possession singular' and 'kingdom singular of priests'; those are the teacher's emphases, not words in the text.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What changes if your daily life, not just your quiet time, is temple service?
2. Where are you conforming without noticing?
3. Which 'mercies of God' from Romans 1-11 move you most toward obedience?
4. Do you tend to inflate or despise your role? Why?
5. Do you know what you were saved for, not only what you were saved from?

## Application
- (video) Paul reminds the church that their lives are not their own (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Grace is for good works God prepared beforehand (Ephesians 2:10), and it extends to the roles He gives. The teacher traces his own assignments: a couple of years removed from being an obnoxious atheist, he taught apologetics to a youth group and caught the teaching bug; he became a public high school teacher in Las Vegas, then a pastoral intern, then a pastor; a dream led his family to Tennessee for full-time ministry. A senior pastor once told him, 'Nate, I don't know what to do with you.' Through pain and betrayal, God broke him to fill him with humility, and he is only now understanding Romans 12:3.
- Study note (added): write down one role God has given you this season (at home, church or work). Next to it, write one way to serve in it this week with 'sound thinking' (12:3): neither inflating nor despising it.
